messages:
maya: FYI — after last night's KMS rotation some projects with the 'Project Reader' role-alias are showing EDIT buttons in the Console. Saw it on staging and two prod tenants :rotating_light:
sean: Can you repro? steps + a quick curl would help.
maya: Repro steps i used:
1) impersonate service account for project-x
2) GET /v1/projects/project-x -> returns roles: [\"reader\"]
3) Console UI hides edit (expected) but PATCH still succeeds and changes apply 
4) reproducer curl below
```
TOKEN=REDACTED
curl -i -X PATCH https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/project-x \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"name\":\"test-change\"}'
```
sean: whoa. So UI gating is working but API enforcement is not. Are audit logs captured for those PATCHes?
alex: checking logs now — we have a small cluster of KMS Decrypt failures around the rotation window. When decrypt fails, role_mapper currently falls back to legacy mapping path which resolves to an editor-equivalent for some legacy projects. That explains the UI/API mismatch.
jen: Do the audit entries show the actor for those requests? If actor is null we lose attribution.
maya: audit created but actor null for ~8 requests during the window. snippet:
```
{
  \"action\":\"project.update\",
  \"actor\": null,
  \"service\":\"console\",
  \"resource\":\"projects/project-x\",
  \"meta\":{\"role_check\":\"failed_kms_decrypt\",\"request_id\":\"req_02f9\"}
}
```
rbac-bot: alert: role-mapper-decrypt-errors spike: count=8 timeframe=8m severity=high
ops-bot: automated: KMS key rotation completed @2026-03-19T04:12Z — 8 decrypt errors detected between 04:12 and 04:20 UTC
sean: mitigation idea: treat KMS Decrypt errors as DENY instead of fallback. Can we hot patch role_mapper to fail-closed?
alex: agree. I'll open a tiny PR to change Decrypt error handling to fail-closed and return 403 for protected endpoints. Pushing now.
jen: I'll open an incident (INC-2026-0042) and add timeline + affected customers. Also will run a reconciliation job to find any changes applied during the window where actor==null.
maya: dug into heap dump — role_alias cache TTL expired and the refresh call hit a KMS decrypt that timed out. So the service fell back to old mapping logic. Reproducer above works consistently if you kill KMS responses for a short period.
sean: after the fail-closed patch we should run a backfill: map request_id -> token logs to populate missing actor fields and then mark those audit events as completed. Also a postmortem.
alex: I'll add an extra audit field in the patch: \"effective_roles\" containing computed roles at time-of-request (so future forensic can reconstruct intent even if decrypt fails).
jen: action items: 1) alex: PR to treat Decrypt errors as deny (ETA 30m) 2) jen: incident open + run scan to list affected tenants (ETA 20m) 3) ops: verify KMS rotation health + re-run rotation checks (ETA 1h) 4) maya: run repro across 5 tenants and post results (ETA 45m)
maya: assigned and running tests now, will post results to the incident channel. :thumbsup:
sean: great. once alex's patch is live we should throttle any automated rotation jobs until we validate no more decrypt spikes.
alex: PR merged to canary, enabling fail-closed. Watching metrics.
ops-bot: automated: canary rollout completed to 2 nodes.
maya: quick check — canary nodes blocked the PATCH as expected and audit actor populated correctly for denied attempts.
jen: thanks team. i'll start the postmortem doc after we finish the backfill.
sean: thx — keeping an eye on audit and KMS metrics. :eyes:
